## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Āpídámó Jùshě Shìlùn* 阿毘達磨俱舍釋論 (CBETA T29n1559) is the Chen dynasty (陳) translation of Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya*, in 22 juan, composed by Vasubandhu 婆藪盤豆 ([婆藪槃豆菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A9%86%E8%97%AA%E6%A7%83%E8%B1%86%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9)) and translated by Paramārtha 真諦 ([真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6)). It is the older of the two surviving Chinese translations of the *Kośa*, predating Xuanzang's version ([KR6l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0023), T1558) by approximately a century. The title *Shì-lùn* 釋論 emphasizes the "commentary" (*bhāṣya*) character of the text.

**Abstract**

Paramārtha 真諦 (499–569 CE) translated the *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya* sometime in the mid-6th century, most likely in the period 563–567 CE during his stay in Guǎngzhōu 廣州. His translation, in 22 juan (shorter than Xuanzang's 30-juan rendering), became the first complete Chinese translation of the *Kośa* and was widely studied in southern China. Paramārtha's rendering was criticized by later scholars — notably 普光 [普光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E5%85%89) in his commentary ([KR6l0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0034)) — for occasional errors and archaic terminology. Xuanzang undertook his fresh translation ([KR6l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0023)) partly in response to these perceived shortcomings.

The text belongs to the same stratum of Sarvāstivāda scholasticism as its pair-text ([KR6l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0023)): both translate the same Sanskrit source, but the two renderings reflect different translation methodologies (Paramārtha's more fluid, Xuanzang's more literalistic). Vasubandhu's dates and the relationship between the "Sarvāstivāda Vasubandhu" (author of the *Kośa*) and the "Yogācāra Vasubandhu" (author of the *Triṃśikā* etc.) remain debated in modern scholarship.
